question: Which comparison does the hipfire attribute graph apply to IncreasePerShotFraction, and what are the unnamed comparison functions used across the graphs?

sourceFacts.method: Compiled expression graphs were listed with expression-graphs/exgraph.py (format from L4016, names from L4017 and L4019) and read section by section by a delegated reader; each constant cited here was then checked at its raw offset in the resource file. Full reading: expression-graphs/findings/native-function-names.md.

control.description: Every cited constant is a raw-offset check against the resource body. Function meanings marked inferred in the findings file are not relied on for the checked values.

points: Hipfire (`WeaponAttributesConfig_HipfireAttributeDelegate`, 0x20 to 0x68): factor = 1.2 if `IncreasePerShotFraction` != 1.0 else 1.0, then x 0.425 inside the square root. The site's rule (1 at the base value, sqrt(1.2) otherwise) is the same; any departure from 1.0 selects 1.2.
`c07cd1f5` is float not-equal: less-than and greater-than are other identifiers, and less-or-equal would give 1.2 at the base value, which the site's verified cases rule out.
`16f0b3aa` is read as float equal; `7072f0cc` integer not-equal; `c22c64f8` integer greater-than; `bb9ecb3e` integer greater-or-equal; `f78bc893` integer less-or-equal; `a46ea4fe` integer subtract.
The reader (`exdis.py`) and NOTATION.md carry the names with a question mark; evidence per function is in the findings file.
33,083 candidate names under four hash functions matched no identifier, and the graph source assets hold no node list.

inference: All names except float not-equal rest on usage patterns (constants compared, guard and chain idioms), not on a decoded definition.
`f78bc893` could be strict less-than; `c22c64f8` is taken as greater-than because not-equal is already assigned.
unresolved: About 600 other function identifiers remain unnamed; the 20 most frequent are slot and handle accessors.
Listings on disk were generated before these names were added; regenerate to see them.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Seven more native functions named from use; the hipfire graph's comparison is float not-equal, so the 1.2 factor applies whenever IncreasePerShotFraction differs from 1.0
leads.summary: Function identifiers are not reversible name hashes, so seven functions were named from usage across 1,010 listings: float not-equal and equal, integer not-equal, greater, greater-or-equal, less-or-equal and subtract. The hipfire graph applies float not-equal: factor 1.2 when `IncreasePerShotFraction` differs from 1.0, else 1.0, inside the square root. This matches the site's inferred condition and settles its direction. 3 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: A graph is found where one of these names gives a wrong result against a measured or site-verified value.
leads.statusNote: Seven functions named; hipfire comparison settled.
